A.name: Editorial Authority
A.notes: Wants a framed subject rather than a full-bleed wash, and prefers a restrained height — a full-viewport hero fights the 'considered' read. Proof arrives as an award/logo marquee. Exemplar: A-cinematic-authority.md (light-weight 300 display is the cinematic sub-reading). EXEMPLAR: references/exemplars/A-cinematic-authority.md. Read it at Stage 4 alongside this contract - the transform gives you the tokens, the exemplar gives you the section flow, the DST mapping and the honest can't-do list. Added 3.01, when an audit found that 11 of 13 contracts named no exemplar at all.
A.paletteIntent: paper/ink: light body-bg, near-ink text, ONE sparing accent on links/pretitle

header.why: Editorial authority is announced by the wordmark, not by chrome. No glass — a hairline rule under a solid header is the whole treatment.

cards.__path: section c-cards / c-card-item attributes + theme.elements (radius inherits transform.layout.default-radius)
cards.border: a single hairline at 10-14% ink, all four sides
cards.padding: generous — 3.2rem+, the whitespace is the authority
cards.gridCaution: A prefers long-form; a 4-up grid of one-line cards reads thin. Two columns with real copy beats four with labels.
cards.why: Editorial authority is carried by measure and restraint, not by surfaces. A filled tile competes with the type; a hairline lets the grid read as a table of contents.
cards.evidence: A-cinematic-authority — 3-up capability cards, stats pulled into a counter row

composition.evidence: A-cinematic-authority.md (measured): the close is a full-bleed dark band with backgroundOverlay, one headline, an audience list and a single partnership CTA; the footer is the 'Join the Mission' CTA line + contact + socials (footer.md #3, not a wordmark). Proof arrives as press/approvals, so quote cards take logos rather than avatars. accentDensity lowered from the inherited 'medium' to match A's own decorationFamily — 'rule/hairline + generous whitespace; no glow'.

B.name: Conversion Engine
B.notes: The intake path is the point: it needs somewhere to put two actions plus reassurance. Counters are its signature proof. Exemplar: B-conversion-fintech.md (accent reserved for the primary action only). EXEMPLAR: references/exemplars/B-conversion-fintech.md. Read it at Stage 4 alongside this contract - the transform gives you the tokens, the exemplar gives you the section flow, the DST mapping and the honest can't-do list. Added 3.01, when an audit found that 11 of 13 contracts named no exemplar at all.
B.paletteIntent: dark hero band + bright brand accent reserved for CTA fills; supply the full -alt set (R15)
B.decorationFamily: A directional GLOW behind the CTA cluster — kind:'blur', not an SVG motif. A grid (blueprint/plus) may sit under it on the dark band.

header.why: Sticky WITHOUT hide-on-scroll: B's header carries the CTA, so it must never leave. Solid sticky background so the button stays legible over any band.

cards.border: none — the fill IS the edge
cards.gridCaution: none — the card grid is B's natural unit.
cards.why: Conversion wants the card to look pressable. A pale tint fill plus a per-card link is what makes a 3-up read as three choices rather than three paragraphs.
cards.evidence: B-conversion-fintech — loan-program cards, image + body + per-card "Discover" link, pale-blue fills at secondary-color3/4

Two alternating l-content-2 bands plus the Borrowers/Brokers 2-up out of ~8 sections ⇒ 0.35. One small brand motif is the only ornament on the page, hence 'low'. cards.why: F's whole contract is restraint — 0px radius, flat bands, tonal-wash imagery. A filled card is the single fastest way to make a luxury page look like a template. Default to no surface and let the hairline and the measure do it.
cards.evidence: F-monochrome-botanical — image-led product cards (showMedia:true, showIcon:false, image-above), price as subtitle, 3-up

G.name: Playful Rounded / Friendly Local
G.notes: Radius is doing the emotional work and it should be the largest of any archetype — pill buttons, big rounded cards. Trust arrives as a rating/review strip, not an award marquee. Condensed or severe faces break it. ONE exemplar with TWO sub-variants: references/exemplars/G-playful-rounded.md — **vivid** (default; full-chroma accent as button and badge fill, measured on ohanastudentservices.com, itself a DST build, and on azbenefitco.com at lower chroma) and **subtle** (the same structure desaturated, for grief/cremation/hospice/elder-care/health/veterinary, measured on birdsongcremations.com). Structure is fixed and saturation is the only dial — see transform.subVariants for the deltas. Cheerfulness is wrong in the subtle categories, and pushing them into C loses the pill-and-rounding that makes them approachable. **Where the playfulness actually lives (2.73, measured on Ohana):** in BUTTON AND ICON GEOMETRY, not in background motifs — a 50px pill whose label is ink on the accent, carrying a 36px circular icon badge in the DEEPER accent, repeated 8 times, plus 30 inline SVGs. Ohana runs four of six bands on one base and introduces colour exactly twice, each time behind a shaped band edge. So G is not 'tint every other band'; it is a quiet ground with loud interactive elements. accentDensity stays 'high' pending Olha's call — R196 counts background decorations, and on this evidence the count may be measuring the wrong instrument.
G.paletteIntent: bright but soft primaries on a light base; a SECOND bright accent for variety rather than one sparing accent
G.decorationFamily: soft rounded blobs / friendly dot cluster, mid opacity — BUT see notes: all three measured G references carry playfulness through pill buttons + circular icon badges + icon density, and Ohana uses shaped band edges rather than background motifs. Prefer interactive-element geometry first; reach for background motifs only when the page still reads flat.

header.why: Friendly and out of the way. Glass optional; a soft translucent row suits the rounded register.

cards.__path: section c-cards / c-card-item attributes + theme.elements (radius inherits transform.layout.default-radius)
cards.gridCaution: none — G forbids the hairline grid, so always give the card a fill.
cards.why: Playful rounded reads through the radius and the fill together. At 28px a hairline looks like a mistake; the filled pill-card is the archetype.
cards.evidence: G-playful-rounded — 3-up icon-led pillars with borderRadius:"large" resolving to the authored generous radius; proof strip via titleIsCounter (counter row in vivid, rating strip in subtle). In vivid, cards may invert against a tinted band via a per-card backgroundOverlay rather than taking a tint of their own.

H.paletteIntent: near-neutral desaturated base that gets out of the way of real photography; ONE accent reserved for CTAs only
H.decorationFamily: none — the photograph is the decoration; at most a hairline caption rule

header.why: Hide-on-scroll so the photography gets the full viewport. Glass ON is genuinely useful here — the header sits over full-bleed images.

cards.padding: the scrim carries it — 2.4rem inside the overlay
cards.gridCaution: H forbids icon cards and hairline grids. If there is no photograph for a tile, H does not want a card there.

I.name: Brutalist / Raw Structural
I.notes: Flatness is the point: the accent is a SOLID fill, never gradiented or tinted, and decorations are hard rules/borders rather than soft SVG motifs. Reads as a mistake for trust-first/regulated verticals. NO EXEMPLAR YET (BACKLOG gap). EXEMPLAR: references/exemplars/I-brutalist-flat.md. Read it at Stage 4 alongside this contract - the transform gives you the tokens, the exemplar gives you the section flow, the DST mapping and the honest can't-do list. Added 3.01, when an audit found that 11 of 13 contracts named no exemplar at all.
I.paletteIntent: maximum contrast and FLAT — near-black ink on paper (or the inversion); exactly ONE saturated accent as a solid fill, never gradiented
I.decorationFamily: hard rule/border blocks (visible 2-4px), a divider bar; no soft motifs, no glow

header.why: Static with a hard visible border. Brutalist chrome does not float, blur or animate — glass and hide-on-scroll are both wrong.

cards.__path: section c-cards / c-card-item attributes + theme.elements (radius inherits transform.layout.default-radius)
cards.border: a hard 1-2px ink rule, full opacity, all four sides
cards.gridCaution: none, but zero-gutter is the point — I is where a raw grid with visible rules belongs.
cards.why: Brutalist wants the structure visible. 0px radius, a real rule rather than a tint, imagery:none in the surface contract. A soft fill hides exactly what the archetype is showing.
cards.evidence: I-brutalist-flat — columnsDesktop:2 case-study cards at borderRadius:"none", card head 30px fw 500

J.name: Organic / Biophilic
J.notes: Calm and low-saturation: no neon, no hard edges. Either a real nature/lifestyle image OR a solid earth band carrying a botanical decoration motif — the motif is the throughline. Generous band rhythm (Density low, §2a). NO EXEMPLAR YET — high SBS value (landscaping/wellness/eco). EXEMPLAR: references/exemplars/J-organic-biophilic.md, references/exemplars/J-organic-biophilic.md (kolenda = DARK reading, melinegobet = LIGHT reading; they are further apart than the shared letter suggests). Read it at Stage 4 alongside this contract - the transform gives you the tokens, the exemplar gives you the section flow, the DST mapping and the honest can't-do list. Added 3.01, when an audit found that 11 of 13 contracts named no exemplar at all.
J.paletteIntent: desaturated earth base — forest/sage green, stone, warm sand/cream body-bg; accent a warm amber/clay. Low saturation, no neon
J.decorationFamily: botanical leaf/organic-line motif at readable opacity — the throughline

header.why: Quiet and retreating. A translucent sticky background over the sand base; glass optional.

cards.__path: section c-cards / c-card-item attributes + theme.elements (radius inherits transform.layout.default-radius)
cards.gridCaution: **The important one.** J forbids hairline grids and counter tiles, and its exemplar deliberately does NOT use a card grid for services — it runs six l-content-2 bands, because a consultative offer needs a paragraph plus imagery per item and a grid flattens both. Reach for the grid only when the items are genuinely short.
cards.why: Organic reads through warmth and the botanical line motif, not through structure. Where F removes the surface, J softens it: a warm fill on the 16px radius, and cards on a dark band get an explicit backgroundColor plus inverted:true (R137).
cards.evidence: J-organic-biophilic — c-cards columnsDesktop:1 with feature images; cards on #003635 with inverted:true; services deliberately l-content-2 bands, not a grid

composition.evidence: J-organic-biophilic.md (measured); footer.md #3 names Bart Kolenda as its own source, so J's footer recipe is directly attested. Six l-content-2 service bands plus the project bands ⇒ ~0.45 two-column, far above the inherited 0.3. The CTA is a quiet inline line ('Interested in Seeing More Projects?'), not a band. Surface changes are full polarity flips (hunter green ↔ white ↔ #003635), so no rule is needed between them — divider 'none'; the all-green system carries no warm accent, hence 'low'. testimonialTreatment is UNEVIDENCED: the exemplar has no testimonial band; the inherited value stands until one is measured.
composition.footerRecipeWhy: biophilic motifs at low opacity are already this archetype's decoration language; 10 is that language applied to the footer, and its top-edge wave suits an organic close better than a CTA-led band.

K.name: Aurora / Gradient-Depth
K.notes:
The ONLY archetype whose signature IS the gradient — layered mesh/radial built from the client's REAL brand hues. R126: purple->pink when that isn't the brand palette is the AI-slop default; rebuild from captured hues. A flat gradient alone is the 7/10 failure (R104) — it needs a SECOND layer: grain/dot texture or blurred glow pools. Exemplar: K-aurora-gradient-depth.md, which also shows K can serve a regulated vertical when the gradient stays dark, cool and low-chroma. NO EXEMPLAR YET (BACKLOG gap). **Two readings (2.10):** dark (gradient as a room) and light (gradient as atmosphere behind ink type) — see `readings`. Both must satisfy R104's second layer.

— — — ADDED 3.09 (the original contract above is RESTORED verbatim; the 3.09 pass briefly overwrote it, which destroyed the R126 purple->pink warning, the R104 second-layer requirement and the two-readings note. Three measured sites are ONE INPUT, not grounds for replacing accumulated contract knowledge.) MEASUREMENT (findrealestate.com, rideradian.com, paralleluniverse.com.ua, 1440x900): Radian and Parallel Universe carry ZERO large gradients; FIND carries ONE, a 1440x232 strip of linear-gradient(rgba(255,255,255,0), rgb(255,255,255)). So the gradient is not what these pages are BUILT from — but the sentence above is still right about what K IS, because a gradient is what K's own signature surface looks like. What the measurement adds is the STRUCTURE those pages use to carry it: the SECTION GROUP (see __sectionGroup, R222, recipes/layout-families.md). Treat the two as complementary: the original describes the surface, 3.09 describes the scaffolding. FIRST DRAFT — three sites, one unmeasurable (iff.com/sustainabilityreport), no completed K build. Correct against the first real K page.
K.paletteIntent: deep base carrying layered mesh/radial gradients built from the client's REAL brand hues (2-3 stops); accent is the brand color
K.decorationFamily: grain/dot texture OR blurred glow pools over the gradient — one of the two is REQUIRED; a bare gradient is R104. Glow is often better on a dark cool base (grain bands on cheap displays). Evidence: cybercrest exemplar has 0 texture layers, 11 blur elements, and does not read flat.

header.why: **Glass ON — this is the archetype it was built for.** A frosted header over a gradient mesh is exactly the Aurora read, and a gradient sticky background is supported. Centre the logo for the symmetrical composition.

cards.__path: section c-cards / c-card-item attributes + theme.elements (radius inherits transform.layout.default-radius)
cards.border: a 1px gradient-edge or a light inner glow
cards.mediaMode: none — the gradient is the media
cards.gridCaution: none — K prefers mixed-fill and bento, so heterogeneous tiles are the register rather than a uniform grid.
cards.why: Gradient-depth reads as glass over depth. K is the one archetype where cards-glass-over-media is preferred rather than forbidden; the tint plus a light edge is what makes a tile float on a gradient band instead of sitting on it.
cards.evidence: K-aurora-gradient-depth — c-cards on a light band with inverted:true flipping against the dark base; card head 21.9px fw 500

composition.footerRecipeWhy: gradient depth is the archetype's subject, so the fade-into-footer CTA option is native rather than an effect — the close becomes one field.

L.notes: Polarity rhythm is expressed as COLOUR — alternating solid colour-block bands, not just light/dark. Solid flat primaries, no gradients, no tints, no photo in the hero. Per-tile colour needs ds-column (c-card-item supports.color is null, v2.05). NO EXEMPLAR YET (BACKLOG gap). EXEMPLAR: references/exemplars/L-geometric-modernist.md. L.paletteIntent: a small set of FLAT saturated primaries used as solid colour blocks on white/paper; high contrast, no gradients, no tints

header.why: Static, centred logo, hard rule. A constructivist poster has a masthead, not a floating bar. No glass — L is flat.

cards.__path: section c-cards / c-card-item attributes + theme.elements (radius inherits transform.layout.default-radius)
cards.border: none — colour blocks butt against each other
cards.gridCaution: none — L prefers mixed-fill and bento, so vary the tile fills rather than the tile sizes alone.
cards.why: Geometric Modernist is colour-blocking: flat saturated fills, hard 0px corners, no borders. The differentiation between tiles is HUE, which is why L prefers cards-mixed-fill-grid — and per capabilityVocabulary per-tile colour needs ds-column, not c-cards.

Testimonials are ordinal-numbered ('01 …'). Rhythm is chromatic — bone / terracotta / near-black block boundaries do the dividing, so no rule; one gradient on the entire page ⇒ 'minimal'.

M.name: Luxury Light / Tonal
M.notes: The LIGHT sibling of F. Same argument — restraint is the signal — on a pale tonal ground instead of a near-black one. Added 2.41 because R174 (polarity) correctly failed a real build that declared F and shipped polarity:'light': the concept was not wrong to be light, it was wrong to call itself Dark Glam. Reach for M for wellness, boutique hospitality, skincare, quiet premium DTC, high-end service brands whose equity is calm. Exemplar: references/exemplars/M-luxury-light-tonal.md (2.98) — measured from Airfield La Caminera with cross-readings from Poetic, Vivre, The Bend Club and Reverie Safaris. NOTE: 2.41 wrote this contract from Oura alone and pointed at an exemplar file (oura-luxury-light-tonal.md) that was never written; the pointer was dangling for 57 revisions. The five measured references corrected two things — see __displayWeightReadings on type and the buttons.why.
M.paletteIntent: pale warm-neutral base (bone/oatmeal/cream), ONE muted deep ink for type, and at most one desaturated accent used less often than in any archetype except F. No black.

fonts.secondary: high-contrast didone/elegant serif, used at LIGHT weight — 200-300, never bold

surface.bandBackground: flat or a very soft tonal gradient between two neighbouring pale tones
surface.why: M is the one archetype where a gradient BAND is right, because its exemplar's ground is a barely-there cream-to-pale-blue wash — but only between adjacent pale tones. A two-hue or saturated gradient breaks it instantly. Note this is the band surface; a legibility scrim over a photograph is governed by R178 and is permitted regardless.
surface.__darkPoleNote: R216 (2.98, corrected 2.99). M and F both assume ONE dark pole reused for every inverted band. Three measured references vary it, on two different axes: Airfield alternates ten bands across FOUR darks (#1a1a1a 0deg, #26201a 30deg, #403931 32deg, #192520 155deg) holding lightness at 10-22%; Diamond Rose Sanctuary runs two darks at a held hue (137deg) with lightness moving 11% -> 20%; Creative Marketing runs nine near-blacks inside 0-3% L. ANCHOR ONE AXIS AND VARY THE OTHER - held value + moving hue reads as a set of rooms, held hue + moving value reads as depth. Varying BOTH is the failure mode. Contrast against light text is unchanged either way, so no AA gate moves. Cheapest richness upgrade available to a light-luxury concept.

M.decorationFamily: NONE by default, exactly as F. If one element is used it is a kind:"blur" pool at 0.04-0.08, or the tonal band gradient itself. Never a painted wash, never a technical grid.

header.why: Static and centred as F. UNLIKE F, M keeps a visible CTA pill in the header — its brands are usually transactional (book, subscribe, buy) where F's are often reputational. A luxury-light header with no CTA reads unfinished, which is R179.

cards.surface: none, or a barely-there tint one step off the band
cards.border: a hairline at 8-12% ink, or nothing
cards.padding: very generous — 4rem+, the space is the luxury
cards.gridCaution: Two or three columns (columnsBias [2,3]). For THREE items prefer a 3-up image-led or numbered card row over three stacked l-content-2 bands — see R180.
cards.why: As F, but M tolerates a 3-up where F does not: on a pale ground three quiet cards read as an index, whereas on near-black they read as clutter.
cards.evidence: DERIVED from oura + the immersion reference, not yet exemplified by a built M concept

flows.name: Before / After
flows.bestFor: Visual trades, exterior work, cleaning, remodeling.
flows.avoid: Projects without genuine before/after media.
flows.rhythm: CTA at peak conviction after the reveal, then repeated at close.

flows.name: Feature-Led
flows.tagline: Clear offer, useful detail, decisive close
flows.bestFor: Service and product homepages where the offer is understood.
flows.avoid: Avoid using it for every concept; it is the safe default.
flows.rhythm: Primary in hero, repeated once in the closing band.

flows.name: Hero-Centric
flows.bestFor: Premium consumer, bold trade, or visually-led brands.
flows.avoid: Information-dense offers that need explanation above the fold.
flows.rhythm: One dominant CTA in the hero, one echo at the bottom.

flows.name: Minimal Single-Column
flows.tagline: Headline, proof, three benefits, one action
flows.bestFor: Focused offers and restrained editorial concepts.
flows.avoid: Brands that need breadth or a heavy proof stack.
flows.rhythm: Single-CTA focus; no competing secondary path.

flows.name: Testimonial-Led
flows.bestFor: Trust-first categories and considered services.
flows.avoid: Projects without real testimonial content.
flows.rhythm: Social proof lands immediately before the primary CTA.

flows.name: Trust & Authority
flows.tagline: Mission, proof stack, solution, clear path
flows.bestFor: B2B, enterprise-adjacent, regulated, federal, professional services.
flows.avoid: Playful consumer or urgent local-trade briefs.
flows.rhythm: Nav CTA plus a low-friction close after proof.

flows.name: Portfolio / Gallery
flows.bestFor: Studios, architecture, photography, fabrication, design.
flows.avoid: Offer-led pages where imagery cannot carry the sale.
flows.rhythm: Gallery tiles carry the middle; contact closes.

flows.name: Comparison-Led
flows.bestFor: Concrete differentiators and buyer option evaluation.
flows.avoid: Claims that cannot be substantiated.
flows.rhythm: CTA in the highlighted choice and after objections.

flows.name: Pricing-Led
flows.bestFor: Transparent packages, retainers, subscriptions.
flows.avoid: Custom quote-only services.
flows.rhythm: CTA on every tier plus a closing band.

flows.name: Lead Capture
flows.tagline: One benefit and one form path
flows.bestFor: Quote requests, gated content, newsletter, waitlist.
flows.avoid: Offers that need a full education sequence first.
flows.rhythm: The form submit is the only primary CTA.

flows.name: FAQ / Documentation
flows.bestFor: Help, support, insurance, complex service questions.
flows.avoid: A homepage whose main job is demand generation.
flows.rhythm: Search is primary; contact is the fallback.

flows.name: Marketplace / Directory
flows.bestFor: Directories, aggregators, listings, marketplaces.
flows.avoid: Single-service businesses.
flows.rhythm: Search leads; list-your-business closes.

flows.name: Content-First
flows.bestFor: Newsletters, publications, creators, research brands.
flows.avoid: Quote-led service businesses.
flows.rhythm: One repeated subscribe CTA.

flows.name: Statement Descent
flows.bestFor: Luxury, hospitality, wellness, tonal brands.
flows.avoid: Fast comparison or urgent trade pages.
flows.rhythm: Three statement bands establish pace before explanation.

flows.name: Pinned-Sequence Spine
flows.tagline: One sticky sequence becomes the argument
flows.bestFor: Narrative products, premium services, cinematic long-form.
flows.avoid: Pricing and comparison pages where scanning matters.
flows.rhythm: One pinned stack only; it consumes the motion budget.

flows.name: Experience-Led Journey
flows.tagline: Story, product, proof and action in a richer sequence
flows.bestFor: Hospitality, travel, automotive, lifestyle and experience-led brands that need imagery plus proof.
flows.avoid: Tiny landing pages with only one message.
flows.rhythm: Open cinematically, prove the offer in the middle, remove objections, then close decisively.

flows.name: Service Conversion Journey
flows.tagline: Explain the service, prove it, answer objections, capture demand
flows.bestFor: Service businesses that need both education and a strong lead path.
flows.avoid: Pure portfolio sites with almost no explanatory content.
flows.rhythm: A useful detail stack builds confidence before contact and the final CTA.

flows.name: Product Discovery
flows.tagline: Show the product from multiple angles before asking for action
flows.bestFor: Products, rentals, vehicles, experiences and visual catalogues.
flows.avoid: Single-offer professional services with no visual product story.
flows.rhythm: Discovery leads, detail follows, proof resolves risk, then contact and conversion.

flows.name: Authority + Resources
flows.tagline: Establish authority, explain depth, then give the audience useful next steps
flows.bestFor: B2B, healthcare, finance, federal, consulting and expertise-led organisations.
flows.avoid: Ultra-minimal campaign pages.
flows.rhythm: Authority and evidence arrive before resources, objections and the conversion path.

flows.name: Community + Brand Story
flows.tagline: People, work and culture become the proof
flows.bestFor: Community-led brands, destinations, schools, studios, nonprofits and founder-led organisations.
flows.avoid: Transactional pages where price or comparison is the main decision driver.
flows.rhythm: Story and people lead, useful content deepens trust, and contact closes the journey.

flows.name: Case Study Spine
flows.bestFor: Consultancies and services with a strong proof story.
flows.rhythm: Proof appears after the response, then the CTA closes the story.

flows.name: Local Service Sprint
flows.bestFor: Local services, clinics, and appointment-led businesses.
flows.rhythm: One clear booking path is repeated after trust-building.

flows.name: Product Launch
flows.bestFor: New products, software, and capability launches.
flows.rhythm: The action appears after product proof and again at the close.

flows.name: Mission & Impact
flows.bestFor: Nonprofits, public-interest teams, and mission-led organisations.
flows.rhythm: Evidence makes the invitation credible before the closing band.

flows.name: Event Registration
flows.bestFor: Conferences, workshops, webinars, and live launches.
flows.rhythm: Registration appears in the hero and immediately after the agenda.

flows.name: Before / After Proof
flows.tagline: Show the change, price the change, prove the change
flows.bestFor: Renovation, dental, aesthetics, fitness, restoration and any transformation offer.
flows.avoid: Services with nothing visual to compare.
flows.rhythm: The transformation appears twice: once as one story, once as a body of work.

flows.name: Objection Clearing
flows.bestFor: High-consideration purchases where the visitor arrives sceptical.
flows.avoid: Impulse or low-cost offers.
flows.rhythm: Every doubt is answered before the price is shown.

flows.name: Compliance & Assurance
flows.tagline: Credentials first, capability second, contact third
flows.bestFor: Regulated sectors: legal, financial, medical, security, public sector.
flows.avoid: Playful consumer brands.
flows.rhythm: Authority is established before anything is asked for.

flows.name: Service Menu
flows.tagline: One promise, many services, one booking path
flows.bestFor: Multi-service practices, clinics, agencies and trades.
flows.avoid: Single-product businesses.
flows.rhythm: The menu is scannable, then the page narrows to one action.

flows.name: Founder Story
flows.bestFor: Consultants, coaches, studios and practices built around named people.
flows.avoid: Large organisations with no single voice.
flows.rhythm: The story earns the credibility that the closing band spends.

flows.name: Location & Visit
flows.tagline: Find us, trust us, come in
flows.bestFor: Clinics, showrooms, restaurants, venues and any premises-led business.
flows.avoid: Remote-only businesses.
flows.rhythm: Practical detail is never more than one section away.

flows.name: Feature Comparison
flows.bestFor: Products and platforms sold against a known alternative.
flows.avoid: Categories with no obvious competitor.
flows.rhythm: The comparison sits between the claim and the price.

flows.name: Free-Trial Funnel
flows.tagline: Value in one line, product in three, start now
flows.bestFor: Self-serve software with a trial or freemium tier.
flows.avoid: Sales-led enterprise offers.
flows.rhythm: The same action appears in the hero, mid-page and close.

flows.name: Resource Hub
flows.tagline: Answer the question, then offer the next one
flows.bestFor: Content-led acquisition, education and search-first pages.
flows.avoid: Pages with a single hard conversion target.
flows.rhythm: Utility first; the conversion is an offer, not a demand.

flows.name: Editorial Long-Read
flows.tagline: One argument, told properly, ending in an invitation
flows.bestFor: Thought leadership, manifestos, campaign and brand pages.
flows.avoid: Pages that must convert in the first screen.
flows.rhythm: A single argument developed section by section.

grain-overlay.note: Fine film grain over the whole band. Measured twice in the 2026-07 reference pass (thebendclub.com `.has-grain`, jaeco.fr `.section-grain-overlay`), both as a full-viewport fixed layer. Use at cover position and LOW opacity (0.03-0.07) - grain is felt, not seen. Warms a flat ground and stops a large single-colour band reading as a screen fill; the classic pairing is a pale luxury ground (M) or a near-black (F). Do NOT combine with another cover pattern on the same band.
